clue.text: Prevented son getting killed

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
to top someone is slang for to kill them

explanation.surface: A grim story: someone was stopped in their tracks when their son was murdered.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a thing prevented from happening has been halted before it could go ahead.

clue.text: Jam jar

definitions.meaning: a jam is a tight spot or predicament, as in getting into a fix
to jar is to grate or rub harshly against something

explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward fix, and to scrape is to grind harshly, as jarring does.

clue.text: Dress in unfashionable suit

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
to fit is to suit, as clothes do

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put on a dowdy, old-fashioned suit.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit is a set of clothes, and dress can mean clothing worn.

clue.text: Get shot of stuff?

parts.note: get shot of usually means discard, but here it means take a camera shot of some object

explanation.surface: It reads like advice to throw out clutter.
explanation.definitionFit: A photograph is a picture taken by a camera, a shot of whatever is in view.

clue.text: Dance music is common initially in party

indicators.note: in places the following letters inside the word for party

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word common

explanation.surface: A remark that this kind of dance tune is standard at parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Disco is a style of pop music made for dancing, popular in the 1970s.

clue.text: Poor hen mistreated — one's always beaten

indicators.note: letters treated badly are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A sad farmyard picture of a neglected, ill-used hen.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the hyphenated NO-HOPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is someone with no chance of winning, so a perpetual loser who is always defeated.

clue.text: Name anything that is right? More difficult

parts.note: aught is an old word for anything
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to name anything correct, then complains it's harder.
explanation.definitionFit: A naughtier child is worse behaved and so harder to handle.

clue.text: Shy person limits razzmatazz

indicators.note: the answer is enclosed within the boundaries of these words, straddling the two

explanation.surface: A timid individual keeps the showy glitz to a minimum.
explanation.definitionFit: Hype is extravagant publicity and fuss, the same showy noise as razzmatazz.

clue.text: Rich for life, practically — I lead in commerce

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: practically means nearly all, so the word life loses its last letter
the lead in a word is its opening letter, here of commerce

explanation.surface: Someone vows to be wealthy almost for good, a leader in business.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich can mean abundant or fruitful, as prolific growth is plentiful.

clue.text: Lower theft?

parts.note: lower here is a thing that lows, a cow, so this is stealing cattle

explanation.surface: It looks like a remark about a drop in the crime of stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustling is the stealing of cattle or horses, and cows moo or low.

clue.text: Sailor recalled island and old relationship

indicators.note: called back, so the word for the sailor is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
I is the abbreviation for island on maps

explanation.surface: A seaman remembers an island and a past love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a ratio is the proportional relationship between two quantities.

clue.text: Fashion models? That's their job

parts.note: the clue pretends to be about the fashion industry, but fashion is a verb: these artists shape figures out of stone or clay

explanation.surface: It seems to describe designers or agents working with catwalk models.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculptors fashion, that is form, models and statues in stone, clay or bronze as their profession.

clue.text: Conservative abandons school with hippy, radical way of thinking

indicators.note: radical suggests a drastic overhaul, so the combined letters are thoroughly rearranged
the letter for the Conservative leaves the word school

explanation.surface: A Tory quits a school full of hippies with their radical outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' takes C out of SCHOOL to leave SHOOL; 'radical' rearranges SHOOL with HIPPY.
explanation.definitionFit: A philosophy is a particular system of beliefs or outlook on life.

clue.text: Power leads bad for tablet

indicators.note: leads means comes in front, so the letter for power is placed before the word for bad

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
ill can mean bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: Electricity cables that are faulty, needing replacement by a tablet device.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is a small pressed piece of medicine, the same thing as a pill.

clue.text: Head getting thanks in education carried on

parts.note: main means head or chief, as in main road
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A head teacher is thanked within the education world.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain something is to keep it going, so continued.

clue.text: Newspaper, say, I sat on after one's tidying

indicators.note: after places the lone letter for one behind the word sat in the build

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or journal that speaks for a group
one is the Roman numeral I, with the 's read as has

explanation.surface: Someone sat on a newspaper after tidying up.
explanation.walkthrough: The construction is loose: the clue's words 'I sat on' are split by the extra letter, and 'after' only roughly says where it goes; 'tidying' is the definition, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Organisation is the act of arranging things neatly, which is what tidying means.

clue.text: Those who voted for Trump remain as annoyed about Clinton's front

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters go round the next letter
annoyed means stirred up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order
front points to the opening letter of Clinton's

explanation.surface: Trump voters stay irritated about Hillary Clinton's campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'annoyed' rearranges REMAIN AS into AMERIANS; 'about' puts it round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters in a US election are citizens of the United States.

clue.text: Loving French friend holding diamonds — a symbol of deep affection?

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the friend word wraps round the next letter

parts.note: ami is French for friend
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
a ring is given as a sign of love or engagement

explanation.surface: A Frenchman offers a diamond ring as a sign of love.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits a ring is only one such symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiring means regarding with warm approval, a fond, affectionate attitude.

clue.text: One criticised about old remote

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: about means around, so the pieces go round the letter for old

parts.note: slated means harshly criticised

explanation.surface: Someone is criticised about an old, distant matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an isolated place is far away and cut off from others.

clue.text: Doctor finally is paged and pain unexpectedly is vanishing

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests an unforeseen turn, so the gathered letters come out in a surprising order
finally points to the closing letter of the word Doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor is paged at the end of a shift and the patient's pain suddenly goes away.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something disappearing is fading from view and ceasing to be seen.

clue.text: The BBC is free to support article

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece goes underneath, so the article letter sits on top

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
to untie is to set free

explanation.surface: A statement that the BBC is free to back a news story.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie (or Auntie Beeb) is a British nickname for the BBC, the UK's public broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickname: the broadcaster earned this name for its prim, aunt-like image.

clue.text: Socks containing small animals

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the word for socks goes round the next letter

parts.note: to sock is to hit, so socks means beats

explanation.surface: Little creatures found inside a drawer of socks.
explanation.definitionFit: Beasts is a general word for animals, especially four-footed ones.

clue.text: Lazy star on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: an idol is a star, someone adored by fans

explanation.surface: A celebrity broadcaster who doesn't put much effort into the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an idle person avoids work and is indolent.

clue.text: True, I later composed texts

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are assembled in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that they wrote some messages afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature is the body of written works, so a collection of texts.

clue.text: Starts to examine artwork, say, expressionist left on here?

definitions.text: Starts to examine artwork, say, expressionist left on here?

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: An expressionist painter's unfinished artwork is left on a stand to be examined.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a painter leaves a work on this stand.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the wooden stand an artist rests a canvas on while painting.

clue.text: Lawyer cut cheese

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the word for lawyer loses its final letter

parts.note: a brief is informal for a barrister or lawyer

explanation.surface: A legal professional slices some cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese with a white rind.

clue.text: Play-off times?

parts.note: not a sporting decider: these are the breaks in a theatre performance when the play is off

explanation.surface: It looks like a question about when sporting play-off matches are held.
explanation.definitionFit: Intervals are the pauses between acts of a play, when the performance stops for refreshments.

clue.text: Attacked over messages

indicators.note: over suggests turning something over, so the phrase for attacked is written backwards

parts.note: set on means attacked, as a dog is set on someone

explanation.surface: Someone was assaulted because of things they wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes are short written messages, like a note left on the kitchen table.

clue.text: Scoundrel returning garment not right for Venus?

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for scoundrel is written in reverse

parts.note: a dog is an old term for a rotten fellow

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter for right from the clothing word

parts.note: a dress is a garment

explanation.surface: A rogue sends back a dress that doesn't suit the goddess of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns DOG into GOD; 'not' takes R from DRESS, leaving DESS. The question mark marks Venus as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus is the Roman deity of love, an example of a female divinity.

clue.text: Climbers might step on these large snakes

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes
adders are venomous snakes

explanation.surface: It evokes the board game snakes and ladders, where climbing and big serpents feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladders have rungs that climbers tread on to go up.
